title: portzone.json
description: A port's own install contract for PortZone, at the top of its repository's default branch. Optional: without it PortZone shows the README and the release files.

switch2.description: A separate Switch 2 build (its own release file, folder or .nro): on a Switch 2, each key here replaces the top-level key of the same name. List "switch2" in platform.runs_on.

description.description: Replaces the store's description. One or two sentences: what the game is and what the player must bring.

icon.description: Square PNG or JPEG in this repository, 256x256 or larger, at most 1 MB. Path from the repository root, read from the default branch: "res/switch/icon.jpg".

banner.description: Wide PNG or JPEG in this repository, 16:9 (1280x720), at most 2 MB. Shown at the top of the port's page; keep the middle clear of text, the edges may be cropped.

release.description: Which releases to install from. Omitted: the newest stable release that has every step's file.

prerelease.description: true: prereleases count too. Sphaira always takes them.

binary.description: The .nro the player launches. Its presence means the port is installed.

steps.description: What PortZone does with the release's files, in order; a later step overwrites what an earlier one wrote. Omit when there is nothing to download because a PC tool makes the game.

full_memory.description: Needs a game's memory: title takeover (hold R) or a forwarder, not the Album.

game_data.description: The player's own files. Never link to copyrighted data.

dir.description: Folder every path below is relative to: the port's own folder, or "sdmc:/" when the files go in several top-level folders (a PC build that writes switch/ and mono/).

prepare.description: A conversion before the first play.

where.description: switch: the port converts the inputs on its first start. pc: the player runs a tool on a computer, and the inputs are what it makes.

tool.description: What the player uses to unpack or convert their copy: a web installer, the tool's download page, or a guide (a README section, a wiki page) when there is no tool. PortZone shows the name and the link.

done.description: Files the conversion leaves. When all are present the required inputs count as met, so a player who deleted the original after converting still shows as ready.

generated.description: Files the port writes itself (settings, saves). Shown in the layout so players know they are not missing.

steps.description: What the player does, in order, one action per step.

platform.description: Where the game came from, and which consoles this port runs on.

original.description: What the port was made from: the system the game came out on, PC, or Source for a game whose source code is the starting point (open-source and fan games, source releases). Shown as a tag and used by the Browse filter. Missing one? Add it to this list by pull request.

runs_on.description: Consoles this port's release runs on. Omitted: ["switch"].

sdFolder.description: A folder on the SD card; sdmc:/ is its root.

step.description: One release file: unzip it into a folder, or copy it into one.

asset.description: End of the release file's name, case-insensitive: "sa2.nro", "-switch.zip".

unzip.description: Extract the zip into this folder.

from.description: With unzip: only this folder of the zip, without the folder itself: "bundle/".

copy.description: Put the file in this folder, as it is.

name.description: With copy: the file's name in the folder, when it differs from the release file's.

relPath.description: Relative to game_data.dir, case-insensitive. * and ? work in the last part; a trailing / is a folder.

input.description: Something the player brings. Met when every file of any one option is present.

required.description: false: optional content, like an expansion.

url.description: Only for files their owner gives away, like shareware.

match.description: With a folder path: the folder must hold at least one file matching this, e.g. "*.pck". Only those files are sent or moved into it.

markers.description: With a folder path: files (or folders, ending in /) inside it that prove it is the right one, e.g. ["liblist.gam", "halflife.wad"]. A folder holding them all is found wherever the player put it, and everything in it goes along.

size.description: Exact size in bytes, when only one version works.

sha256.description: Accepted hashes. Checked only for files up to 64 MiB.
